tonight.headline: Jake Ferguson cleared waivers unclaimed. The answer is still no, and now for a better reason.
body: Discount the 76% again. KEI returns still have an incomplete lineup, which is why ESPN shows them at 70.9 against your 119.6. They were editing on Wednesday afternoon and will fill it before Sunday; expect this to walk back towards even.

Nothing of yours plays tonight — your earliest kickoff is Sunday 11:00. Two things are live: the Lamar Jackson offer to Team 13, which is unchanged and re-verified on this snapshot, and the free-agent seat on your bench. The Jake Ferguson question that the last three runs kept deferring has resolved itself, and the resolution is not the one the ownership number implies.

case.label: What actually changed since 04:05
case.body: Jake Ferguson's status flipped from WAIVERS to FREEAGENT. Nine other managers passed on an 82.3%-rostered tight end. The logged decline thesis named exactly this as its falsification condition — 'Ferguson clears to free agency unclaimed, at which point he is free and the question changes entirely' — so it had to be re-opened, and it was.

case.label: Why the answer held
case.body: PFN rank him TE16 and describe the No. 3 job as his real one: 18.6 points per game in the four games CeeDee Lamb missed, 8.9 with Lamb active. Lamb projects 18.8 on this snapshot and George Pickens 14.8, both ACTIVE. His ownership is falling, not rising. The anomaly was real; the player behind it is a touchdown-or-bust streamer.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens appears on a Dallas injury report, at which point Ferguson is the single best free agent in this league and the seat is his the same hour. Or Colston Loveland draws fewer than four targets again in Week 2, which breaks the tight-end thesis and makes a second startable TE a need rather than a luxury.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sunday 11:00, Mexico City — Baltimore kick off then
doFirst.title: Send Team 13: Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson
doFirst.subtitle: Re-verified on this snapshot, not carried. Lamar is still slot 20 on their bench; Josh Allen is still their starter and is not being asked for.

case.label: The slot check
case.body: Done again on the 12:52 file, because this is the error that shipped twice before. Team 13 hold Josh Allen at slot 0 — starting, and not part of this — and Lamar Jackson at slot 20, their bench. In a one-QB league their second quarterback scores them nothing, every week, all season.

case.label: What they gain
case.body: Their weakest starting slot is RB2, where Rachaad White projects 7.6. Tuten projects 10.1. That is +2.5 this Sunday and +40.6 across the season, converting an asset that cannot enter their lineup into one that starts immediately.

case.label: What you gain
case.body: Lamar Jackson projects 20.6 to Trevor Lawrence's 14.8: +5.8 this week and +30.9 on the season at quarterback, your weakest starting position by some distance. You give up a bench running back who has no red-zone role in Jacksonville.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: You are handing a direct competitor a starting running back in a ten-team league, and they are 0-1 and in the same playoff race. If Lamar misses two games the trade is bad and you will have upgraded an opponent for nothing. The offsetting fact: Lamar is not on Baltimore's Wednesday injury report at all, and Jacksonville's backfield is the one Chris Rodriguez keeps taking short-yardage work from.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back, which kills the +40.6 and removes their reason to say yes. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report between now and Sunday.

doFirst.sources: ESPN league file · Russell Street Report (Ravens Wednesday report)
doFirst.copyText: Hi — you're carrying two quarterbacks in a one-QB league and starting Rachaad White at RB2. Would you do Lamar Jackson for Bhayshul Tuten? Straight up. It's the better side of the deal for you on the numbers: Tuten projects 10.1 against White's 7.6, so it's about +2.5 for you this week and roughly +40 across the season, and it costs you a quarterback you can't start behind Josh Allen. I get a QB upgrade, you get a starter. Happy to look at it the other way round if you'd rather.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Any time before Sunday 11:00, Mexico City — both games kick off then
doFirst.title: Add Devaughn Vele, drop Kayshon Boutte
doFirst.subtitle: Carried from yesterday and re-researched today. Free agent, so no waiver priority is spent — and this is the seat Jake Ferguson does not get.

case.label: The role, with a date on it
case.body: Vele is New Orleans' No. 2 receiver because Jordyn Tyson, drafted to be their third, opened the season on injured reserve with a hamstring. DraftKings Network have him holding that job 'for at least the next three weeks'. Week 1 was 7 catches on 9 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown, used both deep and at the goal line.

case.label: The volume behind it
case.body: Tyler Shough threw 56 times in Week 1 — inflated by overtime, but he averaged 34.9 attempts across his last seven games under Kellen Moore. In full PPR a receiver is paid for catches before he gains a yard, and this is a high-attempt offence with a defined vacancy.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Kayshon Boutte is 13.3% rostered, projects 7.6 and is the weakest seat on your roster by any measure. Nothing is being given up.

case.label: Why not Ferguson in this seat
case.body: Because you get one bench seat and Vele has the better claim on it: a defined role with a three-week clock and ownership moving +11.06 in a day, against Ferguson's No. 3 job behind two healthy receivers and ownership moving -0.91. STRATEGY section 4 ranks role above raw ownership, and this is the case that rule was written for.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Chris Olave is ruled out — which sounds like promotion but in practice means New Orleans face the 3rd-ranked defence in the league with a gutted receiver room. Or Vele appears limited on Thursday or Friday. Or he fails to clear six targets in Weeks 2 and 3, which says Week 1 was the overtime, not the role.

action.label: Add Devaughn Vele · drop Kayshon Boutte

whatWentWrong.title: You dropped Matthew Stafford at 07:12 for a running back who is out indefinitely
whatWentWrong.lead: Zach Charbonnet came in and Stafford went out this morning. Charbonnet is OUT with a shoulder injury, reported as indefinite and having started the season on PUP — and this league has no IR slot.

case.label: What it costs
case.body: The lineup map in this league file has slot 21 set to 0. There is no injured-reserve slot, so Charbonnet occupies a live bench seat and projects 0.0 for as long as the shoulder lasts. Your five-man bench is now Tuten, MarShawn Lloyd, Boutte, Mayer and a player who cannot play.

case.label: Why I am not reversing it
case.body: It is six hours old and it is your move, not the log's. The churn rule closes that seat, and reversing an owner decision inside a day is the pattern this log exists to stop. Seattle's backfield behind Kenneth Walker is a real prize if the shoulder is short.

case.label: How it connects to the card above
case.body: It is precisely why the Vele card matters more today than it did yesterday. With Charbonnet frozen, Boutte's seat is the only bench slot left that can be improved at all — which is also why Jake Ferguson, who wants the same seat, loses to Vele rather than sharing the bench with him.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A dated return timeline from Seattle. If it is longer than three weeks, this becomes a seat to reclaim on Tuesday; if he is trending back, he is a genuine stash and stays. I could not find a date, and I am flagging that rather than guessing one.

whatWentWrong.sources: CBS Sports · Field Gulls · ESPN league file

whatWentWrong.title: Yesterday's 'start Stafford over Lawrence' card has been overtaken — by you
whatWentWrong.lead: The 04:05 brief withdrew it and told you to keep Lawrence. At 07:12 you dropped Stafford outright, which retires the question rather than answering it.

case.label: Where that leaves the position
case.body: Trevor Lawrence is your only quarterback, projecting 14.8. Checked against every slot-0 quarterback in this league on this snapshot — Team 13 at 21.8, Jackrabbits 20.0, the rest between 16 and 19 — that is the lowest starting quarterback projection of the ten. There is no longer a bench option and no longer a decision to get wrong.

case.label: Why that raises the stakes on the trade
case.body: It makes the Lamar Jackson offer the single most valuable thing on this brief. It is no longer an optimisation over Stafford; it is the only path from 14.8 to 20.6 at the position where you are furthest behind the field.

case.label: One thing to not do
case.body: Stafford is now on IPADE waivers at 90.9% rostered, clearing Saturday 07:00 UTC. Re-claiming him would cost your season's waiver priority from 3rd of 10, two days after you cut him, to roster a backup quarterback. That is the reversal pattern and the priority rule in the same move.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 declining the Lamar offer outright and Lawrence appearing on a Jacksonville injury report in the same week. Only then does a quarterback claim become a conversation, and even then a free agent comes first.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +40.6 across the season and +2.5 this Sunday — bigger than yours this week, and saying so is what gets the message read.

case.label: Their surplus
case.body: Team 13 carry Josh Allen at slot 0 and Lamar Jackson at slot 20 in a one-QB league. One of those two is worth nothing to them in every week of the season. Meanwhile they start Rachaad White at RB2 at 7.6, the weakest starting slot on their roster.

case.label: Your hole
case.body: Trevor Lawrence at 14.8 is your weakest starting position, and as of 07:12 this morning he is your only quarterback. Lamar at 20.6 is +5.8 a week and +30.9 on the season into the slot where you are furthest behind.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: You are strengthening a 0-1 rival in a ten-team league. Tuten is a real running back and if Jacksonville hand him the goal line this looks worse in a month than it does today. It is still right, because a bench running back in a shallow league is replaceable from the wire and a top-two quarterback is not.

case.label: Where the arithmetic is soft
case.body: The +40.6 and +30.9 are seasonProj differences, and those figures are identical to the 16 September snapshot. If seasonProj is frozen at preseason values, this is priced on August's opinion. The weekly numbers — +5.8 you, +2.5 them — come from this morning's file and are not affected.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back, or trade or drop a quarterback, or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report. He is not on Wednesday's.

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: The tight end who benefits most from Minnesota's quarterback change, and he is free here.

case.label: Why now
case.body: Carson Wentz is starting for Minnesota with Kyler Murray in concussion protocol, against a Chicago defence that allowed 361 passing yards to Bryce Young in Week 1. FantasyLife rank Hockenson as Minnesota's second target behind Justin Jefferson, ahead of Jordan Addison. Ownership is up +1.78.

case.label: Why not yet
case.body: You start one tight end, Colston Loveland holds it, and IPADE's flex is currently filled by Matthew Golden at 10.9 against Hockenson's 10.1. Adding him costs a bench seat that the Vele card has a better claim on, and Vele's role has a three-week clock where Hockenson's is a one-week matchup.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loveland drawing fewer than four targets against Minnesota on Sunday — the stated falsification condition on his hold. Two weeks of that is a role problem, and Hockenson becomes the answer to it rather than a streamer. He is a free agent, so the seat costs no waiver priority whenever you want it.

worthALook.name: Pat Freiermuth
worthALook.lead: The only MONEY-band tight end on this wire, carried forward from yesterday unchanged.

case.label: Why he is flagged
case.body: 20.1% rostered and moving +1.98, which is the wire's MONEY band: low ownership rising fast. TE19 on consensus rank, which is ahead of Michael Mayer at TE25 sitting on your bench.

case.label: The number against him
case.body: Aaron Rodgers projects 11.6 in this file, second-lowest of any starting NFL quarterback here behind only Cam Ward at 10.9. A tight end's week depends more on who is throwing to him than on anything else, and Pittsburgh's passing game is the worst environment on this board. I did not find reporting that changes that.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Two straight weeks of six-plus targets, or Pittsburgh's passing volume rising. Until then he is a name on a list, and the honest reason he is still listed is that I have not found a reason to remove him, not that I have found a reason to add him.

doNotChase.name: Jake Ferguson
doNotChase.lead: The loudest ownership anomaly in this league just became free, and nine managers were right to pass.

case.label: Why it looks like a gift
case.body: 82.3% rostered nationally, a free agent here as of this morning's waiver run, TE13 on consensus rank with a 167.4 season projection, and IPADE's flex takes a tight end — which STRATEGY section 9 says makes a second startable TE genuinely valuable in this league and worthless in Chem. On the ownership signal alone this is the strongest thing on the board.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 18.6 points per game in the four games CeeDee Lamb missed; 8.9 with Lamb active. PFN rank him TE16 against a TE11 draft position and call the No. 3 job 'his real one', behind Lamb and George Pickens, with Ryan Flournoy eating in from below. On this snapshot Lamb projects 18.8 and Pickens 14.8, both ACTIVE. You would be buying the 8.9 version.

case.label: The second number
case.body: His ownership is moving -0.91. The anomaly is a market that is walking away from him, not one that has not noticed him. Compare Devaughn Vele at +11.06 in the same day.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report — at which point Ferguson is the best free agent in the league and the seat is his that hour. Or Loveland's thesis breaking on Sunday, which turns a luxury into a need. He is a free agent now, so neither costs waiver priority; both are worth watching for.

doNotChase.name: Jason Myers
doNotChase.lead: 97% rostered, on waivers, and claiming him would spend your season's priority on a kicker.

case.label: Why he is on the board
case.body: 97.0% rostered nationally — the single highest ownership figure on either wire — and sitting on IPADE waivers clearing Friday 01:00 Mexico City. KEI returns dropped him at 16:56 Wednesday to add Evan McPherson.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: PFN have Jason Myers K9 this week and Cam Little, who you already own, K3. You would be paying your only waiver claim of the season — priority never resets in this league, 3rd of 10 today, last for the rest of the year after — to move down six places at kicker. STRATEGY section 6 forbids spending priority on a streamer in as many words.

case.label: The required comparison, answered
case.body: Little K3 against the best actually available here: Will Reichard K5, Chase McLaughlin K6, Trey Smack K13, Cairo Santos K14, Chris Boswell K17. Nothing on this wire beats him and nothing is close. Fifth consecutive run this has come back hold.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Cam Little finishing outside the top 20 kickers across Weeks 2 to 4. Even then the replacement comes from free agency, never from a claim.

doNotChase.sources: Pro Football Network · ESPN league activity log

doNotChase.name: Matthew Stafford
doNotChase.lead: You cut him six hours ago. He is on waivers at 90.9% rostered. Leave him there.

case.label: Why he will look tempting on Saturday
case.body: 90.9% rostered, projecting 17.4 against Trevor Lawrence's 14.8, clearing waivers Saturday 07:00 UTC. ESPN's projection prefers him and it will keep preferring him all week.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: The cost is not the projection, it is the priority. One claim moves you from 3rd of 10 to last for the entire season, and you would be spending it on a backup quarterback you personally dropped two days earlier. That is the reversal pattern and the priority rule broken in a single move, and this log records both as having cost real points before.

case.label: The read underneath it
case.body: Three of four expert boards read on 17 September rank Lawrence ahead of Stafford despite ESPN's +2.6 — Fantrax QB9 to QB14, WalterFootball, Lindy's start/sit. Where ESPN's projection and current reporting disagree here, believe the reporting.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing that involves a claim. If Lawrence is ruled out and the Lamar trade has been declined, the answer is a free-agent quarterback — Bo Nix at 84.5% rostered is free on this wire — not a waiver claim.

settled.result: He did not go unclaimed here. Boutte is still on your bench and is the drop in today's Vele card instead.

cannotSee.label: Whether Team 13 have read the offer
cannotSee.body: There is no PROPOSE button — this league's trade write is unmapped, so the card gives you the message and you send it in ESPN. I cannot see whether it was sent, opened or ignored. If it is still unanswered by Friday, the read on that manager's willingness is what changes, not the arithmetic.

cannotSee.label: Brock Bowers's Friday designation
cannotSee.body: He did not practise Wednesday, which is what keeps Michael Mayer on your bench this week. Pete Carroll is quoted expecting him to play against the Chargers while Schefter has the Raiders hoping he misses only one game and a physician reading the same meniscus trim disagreeing. Friday decides it and Friday has not happened.

cannotSee.label: Zach Charbonnet has no return date
cannotSee.body: Reported as out indefinitely with a shoulder after starting the season on PUP. I could not find a dated timeline from Seattle. That matters because with no IR slot in this league he is costing a live bench seat, and the decision to keep or reclaim that seat depends on a number nobody has published.

cannotSee.label: Twelve of your fourteen matchup tiles are not researched
cannotSee.body: I graded two this run: Baltimore against New Orleans, and Denver against Jacksonville. Kansas City, Tennessee, Indianapolis, Green Bay, Minnesota, the Jets, the Chargers and Arizona are dashed because I did not study them, not because they came back average.

cannotSee.label: Season projections may be frozen at preseason values
cannotSee.body: The Lamar arithmetic produces exactly the same +40.6 today as on the 16 September snapshot, from identical seasonProj figures a day apart. That is consistent with a weekly refresh and equally consistent with a preseason artifact that has never updated. The weekly projections in this brief come from this morning's file and are unaffected; every season number should be read as narrowing the list, not settling it.

cannotSee.label: Rival pending claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own. Jake Ferguson at 82.3% and Devaughn Vele at 48.5% and rising are both free agents right now, and either can be gone before you open this.
